title: Genuine cross-frequency coupling networks in human resting-state electrophysiological recordings (Siebenhuehner et al., 2020): SEEG and MEG connectomes (derivative)
description: This derivative dataset repackages the public Dryad release accompanying Siebenhühner et al. (2020). It provides per-subject connectivity matrices computed from 10-minute resting-state SEEG (59 epilepsy patients) and MEG (19 healthy participants, plus a 10-participant eyes-open/eyes-closed cohort) recordings. The matrices cover phase synchrony (PLV, wPLI), cross-frequency phase synchrony, phase-amplitude coupling and amplitude-envelope coupling, each with surrogate values. Supporting files, neuropsychological scores and figure plot data are also included. Raw recordings are not included.
methods_description: SEEG was recorded for 10 minutes at 1000 Hz, eyes closed, with a 192-channel system. Contacts were localised to the Destrieux atlas and referenced to the closest white matter. MEG was recorded for 10 minutes, eyes open, with a 306-channel Elekta/MEGIN system, then processed with tSSS and ICA and source-modelled to 200 parcels with fidelity weighting. Morlet wavelet decomposition (m=5) covered about 1-315 Hz, and coupling matrices were computed per subject and frequency (pair) with surrogate counterparts.
